title: Impressions Of The Shield Hero [Part 3]
paragraphs: “What on earth are you talking about?”
“Oh? Melty, huh.”
Melty showed up just then to check in. Pretty rare.
“Filo-chan asked me to see if the Spear Hero disappeared.”
“You know already. He’s deep into his bard phase.”
“…Seems like it.”

Melty clearly tries not to listen to Motoyasu’s stories—more like, she holds them in contempt. She used to come by fairly often to listen on Filo’s behalf, but one day she just stopped. If I remember right, Motoyasu had been going on about the revolution in Melromarc. And then he said she fell for me and went into heat. She turned bright red and flatly denied it. Since then, she hardly ever comes during this time. Still, knowing Melty’s personality, I can’t say it’s entirely impossible—that’s my take, anyway. She’s the type who dreams of a prince. She’s weak to heroic acts done without regard for profit or loss. Maybe that’s how I was in another world, but the current me is driven by cost-benefit.
“You’re still listening to that ridiculous story, Naofumi?”
“This is my village. I’m the lord. Why should I have to leave because of Motoyasu?”

Honestly… I feel like Motoyasu’s adding a lot of fiction. I don’t want to use spirit magic to check if it’s true. Something about it just feels unpleasant. Why the hell would I be the one confessing to Sadeena? And then that she loves Motoyasu on top of that? That’s the worst. I’d rather avoid confirming that at all costs.
“Just go home already, Motoyasu. You’re causing trouble all over.”
Including Meslion—everything’s a nuisance. Filo’s probably grumbling about not being able to come hang out here too.
“Understood!”
With that, Motoyasu headed off back to the three Filolials.
“Muu.”
“Finally over?”
“That story wasn’t very interesting.”

Well, all three of those Filolials haven’t had a role lately. Of course they’d find it boring. And come to think of it, the only one targeting Motoyasu now is that Yuki girl or whatever. From Motoyasu’s point of view, maybe that’s ideal? Oh yeah, wasn’t it that to him, Filolials are all equally lovable, but the ones he truly adored were Filo and Fitoria?
“Come on, come on! You three go to bed already!”
“Naofumi—Gaelion won’t give up! I’ll become a Raf and win your heart! Until then I’ll protect my virginity!”
“Drop dead!”
Still, I’ll give her points for the determination to become a Raf species just to win my heart. Maybe I can play around with her a little. Strictly as a small animal, though.
“Man… but if that kind of future was possible, I don’t actually hate the story about going to Faubrey and what came after,” Ren murmured as he watched Motoyasu leave.
“But we’re getting killed at completely joke-level timing.”
Itsuki replied calmly—though a little exasperated.
“Well… yeah. If you just ignore that part, it’s fine. I’m just glad Wyndia didn’t hear the part where he said he should’ve killed his own daughter too…”
Ren looked relieved. But sorry, I’m pretty sure she heard that. The villagers love to gossip.
“Even Eclair was surprised when she showed up in Motoyasu’s story.”

Oh yeah, that female knight who started managing a territory after copying me and hasn’t been around much since. Even so, she still shows up when she has time and listens in. When she heard about how she died in prison after being tortured, she made a weird face. She said it was a future that could’ve easily happened if one thing had gone differently. In that sense, she mumbled that my evilness may have kept her alive, and Ren made a weird face at that. Is she brainwashed or something? I was supposedly the culprit, too.
“It really does feel like this moment only exists because of a series of miracles.”
“That’s right, Itsuki-sama.”
“I won’t deny that…”
It’s not like I’m making excuses after the fact, but when it comes to the Prado Desert, maybe I should say it was already cleared? All that treasure buried there… that’s info Motoyasu dropped later.

In reality, when that damn goddess barged into this world, she handed out gear to reincarnators and otherworlders that might’ve been useful. Thanks to Trash’s efforts, we managed to snatch a few weapons, but most of them were destroyed by that goddess’ magic before they could reach us. Thinking that we might’ve hit the jackpot if things had gone well just makes it all the more frustrating.

Then there was the XP collection device-slash-demon maker. That thing went silent once the damn goddess was destroyed, and later, Raphtalia felt a flow of power and smashed it. Well, there were other problems too, but most of them have been dealt with.
“Rafuu.”
“Oh, Raf-chan!”
I petted Raf-chan, who’d been quiet the whole time, while watching off Ren and Itsuki.
“Alright, we’re bothering big bro. Atla, time to go.”
“Ahh, Naofumi-samaaa!”
Fohl took Atla along with him. Those two are as noisy as ever. Now I just need to take care of anyone who hasn’t eaten—like Filo—and clean up the dishes before moving on to the next task.
“But what caught my attention in Motoyasu’s story was Raphtalia turning into a Raf species—”
“That happened because I used spirit power. I’m absolutely never doing that again.”

Hmm… Raphtalia picked up on it. But if the inside is still Raphtalia and she’s in Raf form, wouldn’t that be perfect? Of course, her current form is still included in that, but in a way, that might be the ideal form. Back when I was consumed by the cursed shield, could it be that the ideal version of Raphtalia I envisioned ended up being like that? Considering Raf-chan’s powers, it’s not out of the question.
“Rafuu.”
“Raphtalia, I want to try sleeping with the Raf species version of you as a body pillow.”
“Please, drop that line of thought.”
Hmmm… is it really that unpleasant? Either way, she’s still Raphtalia.
“And then there’s Raphtalia’s friend…”
Rifana, was it…? The girl who died, who had been with Raphtalia back during the slave days. A slave from this village who I wasn’t able to save…

Honestly, I think it’s amazing she could come to terms with her own death and see Raphtalia off. If it were me, I might’ve resisted even in death and chosen to survive—even if I had to rewrite the entire world.

…Well, maybe you can’t know that until the moment comes. In Motoyasu’s story, the me that appeared refused to rewrite the world for his sake and chose to see him off. I thought I understood who I was as a person, but I’m also aware that I’m shaped by my environment. If back when I was tricked by that witch, Motoyasu, Ren, or Itsuki had believed me, maybe my personality would’ve softened a bit.
…No point in thinking about that now.
“Could’ve, should’ve” is just a meaningless hypothetical.
I look over at Raphtalia.
“You weighed your friend’s life against a guaranteed way to kill that damn goddess, huh?”
“…Yes. I’m sorry, Naofumi-sama.”
Raphtalia quietly bowed her head to me.
“Don’t worry about it. If there had been another way, that choice might not have been a bad one… though there might’ve been a lot of sacrifices.”

It wasn’t a decision for me to make, and when I think about what happened, I don’t think it was wrong. I think we could’ve won for sure, but you never know what’ll happen in a fight. If we failed to kill that damn goddess, the world would’ve been destroyed, so in that sense, it was definitely the safer move.
“More than that… I’m sorry I made you go through such a painful decision—and a painful farewell.”

Being reunited with someone you thought was dead, only to say goodbye again… I’ve been through that too. That was Atla. The heart-wrenching pain I felt then—Raphtalia has gone through that twice, including with Atla.
“…Seriously, that idiot Motoyasu really pulled something outrageous.”

If it were true, given the situation, I wouldn’t blame Motoyasu too much, but I still feel like complaining. And on top of putting her through something that intense, he went on to show Raphtalia more horrible things afterward. He had Itsuki do his own tasks, made me buy a different slave from Raphtalia. So, back then, I think I ended up buying that rabbit-looking one.

If Ren was in charge, it would’ve been some kind of lizardman mutt? Feels like I was being steered into awakening to something… concerning. Both would’ve ended up turning into voluptuous beauties like Filo anyway.

I mean, couldn’t he have just asked the slave trader to only push Raphtalia to me? Motoyasu really is an idiot… well, it’s easy to say that in hindsight. Actually, Raphtalia being so stubborn is part of the problem too.

Tracing it back… maybe it’s my fault? Then, after being cornered by Motoyasu and not buying any slaves, he thought Raphtalia was stolen from him, like how far was he planning to push me? To top it off, I didn’t buy any slaves and ended up looking like I was in a mutual love relationship with Sadeena, and showed through my actions that the world could be saved even without Raphtalia. No wonder he hates Motoyasu. Totally justified.
Too many pointless detours!
“It’s understandable why your relationship’s so strained. It must’ve been rough.”
“Yes, it was really hard!”
I feel deeply sorry for Raphtalia. For now, I’ll just pat her head and comfort her. I gently rub Raphtalia’s head.
“Rifana-chan, huh…”
Just as the mood started to lighten up a bit, Keel folded his arms and let out a groan.
Tch… When did he come back?
“How’s she been doing?”
“Well… the last time I saw her, she gave me a push forward.”
“Rifana-chan was such a kind kid. Thinking about others more than herself—amazing.”
“Thinking about it makes me want to see her again… but we can’t anymore, huh?”
“Tomorrow, let’s go put flowers on the grave we all made. A visit for everyone, and for Rifana-chan.”
“You guys do that regularly since it’s close by.”
The graves of those originally from this village, including Raphtalia’s parents, have been made. Everyone regularly cleans them and visits, so there are always fresh flowers.
“Rafuu.”
“I wonder what she looked like?”
“Umm…”
In response to my question, Raphtalia gestures to Raf-chan with open arms.
“Rafuu.”
Then, Raf-chan hops up and transforms. Taller than Keel, shorter than Raphtalia, brown hair—she gives off a cute vibe.
“Ooh!”
The village slaves, including Keel, let out voices of awe.
“She really does look like Rifana-chan!”
“Amazing!”
“Rafuu.”
Well, even if she’s transformed, Raf-chan’s still Raf-chan. Can’t help that. With a pop, Raf-chan stops transforming immediately.
“Come on, you guys, get to sleep. We’ve got more stuff lined up tomorrow.”
“Okay—”
And with that, the slaves head off. …A strange silence falls over me, Raphtalia, and Raf-chan nearby.
“Like we talked about earlier, it must’ve been rough.”
“Yes.”
For Raphtalia, it must feel like she had to watch Rifana die twice. Even if the second time was a proper farewell.

But… from what Motoyasu said, there’s the idea that even in death, the soul lingers to some degree, and the thing about Raphtalia being in a suspended state. And then there were those ghost-like raccoon and weasel creatures we saw near Sadeena’s secret base.

Putting that together… maybe Rifana, who had lost hope in life, possessed Raphtalia in order to keep her alive—something like that flashes through my mind. Well, maybe that’s a bit too convenient of a theory.
“Yeah… but it’s not all sad things. There were a lot of sad things, but also a lot of happy things, and that’s why we are where we are now.”
“I see…”
If Raphtalia thinks that way, then maybe it really is something to be happy about.
“Right, Raf-chan?”
Raphtalia gazes into Raf-chan’s eyes, tilts her head a bit, and smiles.
“Rafuu!”

Right… Raf-chan gives a happy cry, hops onto Raphtalia’s shoulder, and waves at me. Just like Filo, huh? Hm? …Wait, how does Raf-chan even know what Rifana looked like as she grew up? Did Raphtalia tell her? Now that I think about it, Raphtalia used to be a bit wary of Raf-chan, but that’s softened a lot.
“Well, let’s finish up the rest of the work for tonight. Naofumi-sama.”
“Ah, yeah… the next round of noisy ones will be here soon.”
Well… whatever.
“Rafuu!”
And like that, another night slowly passed.
